Q108239356.label: 2025 Trinidad and Tobago general election
Q108239356.summary: General elections were held in Trinidad and Tobago on 28 April 2025 to elect all 41 members of the House of Representatives. President Christine Kangaloo, on the advice of Prime Minister Stuart Young, dissolved parliament and issued the writs for election on 18 March 2025.

Q5607420.label: 1984 Grenadian general election
Q5607420.desc: General elections in Grenada held on 3 December 1984
Q5607420.summary: General elections were held in Grenada on 3 December 1984, the first after the U.S.-led invasion that followed two coups. The result was a victory for the New National Party, which won 14 of the 15 seats. Voter turnout was 86%.

Q1860604.label: 1946 Dutch general election
Q1860604.desc: election of the members of the House of Representatives
Q1860604.summary: General elections were held in the Netherlands on 17 May 1946, the first after World War II. The Catholic People's Party, a continuation of the pre-war Roman Catholic State Party, remained the largest party in the House of Representatives, winning 32 of the 100 seats.

Q6734844.label: Mahoran status referendum, 1976
Q6734844.summary: A referendum on remaining an overseas Territory was held in Mayotte on 11 April 1976, after the proposal of remaining part of the Comoros was overwhelmingly rejected in a referendum in February.

Q836092.label: 1945 Hungarian parliamentary election
Q836092.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Hungary on 4 November 1945. They came at a turbulent moment in the country's history: World War II had had a devastating impact; the Soviet Union was occupying it, with the Hungarian Communist Party growing in numbers; a land reform that March had radically altered the property structure; and inflation was rampant.

Q296956.label: Rolandas Paksas
Q296956.summary: Rolandas Paksas is a Lithuanian politician who served as the sixth president of Lithuania from 2003 until his impeachment in April 2004. He previously served two terms as the prime minister of Lithuania in 1999 and again from 2000 to 2001, and as Mayor of Vilnius from 1997 to 1999 and again from 2000 to 2001.

Q84027388.label: 2024 Azerbaijani presidential election
Q84027388.summary: Presidential elections were held in Azerbaijan on 7 February 2024. Incumbent president Ilham Aliyev, who has held office since 2003, won a fifth consecutive term with over 92% of the vote, defeating his closest runner-up Zahid Oruj, who obtained just 2% of the vote.

Q1453052.label: Mapai
Q1453052.desc: social-democratic/democratic socialist political party in Israel
Q1453052.summary: Mapai was a Labor Zionist and democratic socialist political party in Israel and the dominant force in Israeli politics before merging into the Israeli Labor Party in January 1968. During Mapai's time in office, a wide range of progressive reforms were carried out, as characterised by the establishment of a welfare state, urban rehabilitation, compulsory education, and new rights in the workplace.

Q110778876.label: 2022 Guinea-Bissau coup d'état attempt
Q110778876.summary: A coup d'état was attempted in Guinea-Bissau on 1 February 2022. A few hours later, president Umaro Sissoco Embaló declared the coup over, he said that "many" members of the security forces had been killed in a "failed attack against democracy".

Q93180.label: Seleucid Empire
Q93180.desc: Hellenistic-era Greek state in Western Asia (312–63 BC)
Q93180.summary: The Seleucid Empire was a Greek state in West Asia during the Hellenistic period. It was founded by the Macedonian general Seleucus I Nicator in 312 BC, following the division of Alexander the Great's Empire, and was ruled by the Seleucid dynasty from Seleucia and later Antioch until its annexation by the Roman Republic under Pompey in 63 BC.

Q58416636.label: Kelly Morrison
Q58416636.summary: Kelly Louise Morrison is an American physician and politician who has served as the U.S. representative for Minnesota's 3rd congressional district since 2025. A member of the Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party, she served from 2019 to 2023 in the Minnesota House of Representatives and from 2023 to 2024 in the Minnesota Senate.

Q3511804.label: George T. Whitesides
Q3511804.summary: George Thomas Whitesides is an American politician and businessman who has served as the U.S. representative for California's 27th congressional district since 2025. He was previously chief of staff at NASA and CEO of Virgin Galactic. He is a member of the Democratic Party.

Q164348.label: Hungarian Revolution of 1956
Q164348.summary: The Hungarian Revolution of 1956, also known as the Hungarian Uprising, was an attempted countrywide revolution against the government of the Hungarian People's Republic (1949–1989) and the policies caused by the government's subordination to the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR). The uprising lasted 15 days before being crushed by Soviet tanks and troops on 7 November 1956. Thousands were killed or wounded, and nearly a quarter of a million Hungarians fled the country.

Q25596.label: Saint Martin
Q25596.desc: French and Dutch island in the Lesser Antilles
Q25596.summary: Saint Martin is an island in Leeward Islands of the Lesser Antilles in the northeastern Caribbean, approximately 300 km (190 mi) east of Puerto Rico. The 87 km2 (34 mi2) island has been divided since 1648 roughly 60:40 between France and the Kingdom of the Netherlands, but the Dutch part is more populated than the French. The northern French part comprises the Collectivity of Saint Martin and is an overseas collectivity of France. The southern Dutch part comprises Sint Maarten and is one of four constituent countries that form the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
